The main takeaway from our work is that
receiver caching can be used to mitigate interference in Wyner's models, and that the MG is the same as in non-interfering networks if the cache memories are large enough.
, in Wyner's circular network model, interference mitigation through caching is possible if and only if the prelog of the cache-memories is sufficiently large.
, in contrast to the case of non-interfering networks, the presence of interference does not prevent receiver-caching from completely mitigating it.
